threads.body: Since these are needed only until we switch to stable rpc semconv the added `OpenTelemetry` argument will become unused. Just this is needed temporarily maybe it would make sense to introduce this more sneakily. For example we could have an internal interface similarly to `SpanKeyProvider` that `AttributesExtractor` and friends could implement and the `InstrumenterBuilder` or `Instrumenter` could use that to supply the `OpenTelemetry` instance. Wdyt?

@copilot Update this existing PR to make semantic convention selection instance-scoped without changing the public RPC factory signatures, following the internal-interface direction suggested in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20474#discussion_r4245367142. Use in-place initialization of instance-owned components, not configured copies. Do not reply to that review thread or resolve it.

Keep the existing public entry points: `RpcClientAttributesExtractor.create(getter)`, `RpcServerAttributesExtractor.create(getter)`, `RpcSpanNameExtractor.create(getter)`, `RpcClientMetrics.get()`, `RpcServerMetrics.get()`, and `RpcMetricsContextCustomizers.dualEmitContextCustomizer(getter)`. Remove this PR's added public `OpenTelemetry` parameters on those factories rather than adding another public configuration API.

Introduce a small internal initialization interface analogous to `SpanKeyProvider` in `instrumentation-api`, and have the relevant RPC components implement it. Supply the owning `InstrumenterBuilder`'s `OpenTelemetry` internally, before schema URL resolution and tracer/meter creation. Cover span-name extractors, attributes extractors, operation-metrics factories, and dual-emission context customizers, including registrations made through instrumenter customizers. Ensure the initialization hook remains visible on the registered metrics factory rather than being hidden by the lambda returned by `OperationMetricsUtil`.

Mutate configuration only during initialization, before the component is used by an instrumenter. Repeated initialization with the same `OpenTelemetry` instance should be harmless; reject rebinding to a different instance instead of changing an already-built instrumenter's behavior. Keep helpers instance-owned wherever configuration differs, including the AWS RPC extractors already changed in this PR. Preserve the existing global/default-backed behavior for standalone use of the public helpers without a builder; that fallback must not prevent their first explicit initialization by a builder.

Handle repository-owned decorators before they hide the internal interface. In particular, `DubboTelemetryBuilder` passes the original `RpcSpanNameExtractor` through client/server span-name customizers before constructing the instrumenter builders. Initialize that original extractor with the owning instance before applying the customizers so a returned wrapping lambda still delegates to a configured extractor. Do not add a general wrapper-discovery framework.

Preserve the PR's instance-scoped RPC and service-peer behavior, consistency between span names, attributes, metrics, units and schema URLs, and the nested legacy child-metrics fix. Service-peer helpers that already need `OpenTelemetry` for mapping configuration can keep it. Leave database, messaging and code conventions unchanged.

Adapt the existing focused tests to exercise real instrumenter initialization and emitted telemetry in legacy-only, preview-only and dual-emission modes with independent `OpenTelemetry` instances. Cover harmless same-instance initialization, rejection of cross-instance reuse without corrupting the first instrumenter, standalone helper behavior, and the affected wrapped span-name path. Update the PR description and relevant CHANGELOG text so they no longer claim callers must migrate these public RPC factories. Commit and push to this PR's existing head branch, preserve its ready-for-review state, and do not open a new PR.

@copilot Revise this PR to initialize the affected RPC helpers explicitly at their construction sites instead of adding generic initialization hooks to `InstrumenterBuilder`. This supersedes the generic-builder-initialization part of https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20474#discussion_r4305536269. Keep the unchanged public RPC factory signatures and in-place initialization, not configured copies.

Remove this PR's generic `OpenTelemetryConfigurable` detection and initialization from `InstrumenterBuilder`, including its constructor, registration methods, build path, and customizer handling. Restore the common builder's behavior without an initialization lifecycle for this temporary RPC configuration.

At repository-owned construction sites, immediately after creating an RPC helper that selects semantic conventions, call its internal initialization method with the owning `OpenTelemetry` instance before registering, wrapping, or using it. A direct cast to the existing internal interface and a call to `internalInitialize(openTelemetry)` is fine. Cover the RPC client/server attribute extractors, span-name extractors, metrics factories, dual-emission context customizers, and module-specific helpers such as `GrpcAttributesExtractor` that would otherwise lose their initialization when the generic hooks are removed. Update the relevant telemetry builders and factories across RPC consumers, including the AWS SDK instance-owned extractor lists. Keep Dubbo's initialization before the client/server span-name customizers wrap the original extractor. Do not add another generic lifecycle, wrapper-discovery framework, or public factory parameter to replace the removed hooks.

Preserve instance ownership, harmless repeated initialization with the same instance, and rejection of rebinding to a different instance. Keep global/default-backed behavior for helpers used without explicit initialization. The accepted limitation is that external callers who compose the public instrumenter and RPC-helper APIs themselves do not get automatic instance-scoped selection unless they explicitly initialize the helpers; do not retain generic builder hooks to cover that case.

Adapt the focused tests, particularly `RpcInstanceSemconvTest`, to the explicit initialization contract rather than relying on `InstrumenterBuilder` to configure helpers. Preserve coverage of independent instances, legacy/preview/dual-emission telemetry, matching schema URLs and metrics, reuse protection, standalone behavior, and wrapped span names. Keep the existing service-peer behavior and nested legacy child-metrics fix, and leave unrelated convention domains unchanged.

Update PR description text if it still claims the common instrumenter builder initializes components automatically. Commit and push to this PR's existing head branch, preserve its current draft/ready state, and do not open a new PR or resolve existing review threads.

replies.body: Implemented in c599c1bc. The generic initialization hooks are removed from InstrumenterBuilder; repository-owned RPC construction sites now initialize their helpers directly, including wrapped extractors, AWS lists, and gRPC’s specialized extractor.

threads.body:
@copilot Revisit builder-managed initialization in this existing PR. The explicit casts and repeated `internalInitialize(openTelemetry)` calls in `GrpcTelemetryBuilder` are too much construction-site boilerplate. Use the existing internal `OpenTelemetryConfigurable` interface so `InstrumenterBuilder` or `Instrumenter` supplies its owning `OpenTelemetry` instance to configurable components automatically.

This is a deliberate reversal of the explicit-construction-site direction in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20474#discussion_r4305706130. That comment's prohibition on generic builder initialization and its accepted limitation for external callers are superseded. Review the earlier builder-based implementation in commits edb42b95aca2b951316fa0f96f5051d2e515c94f and 2b38883e6083c6f7cf1e44f77ecdb1cad621b6f0, and the later reversal in c599c1bc4e2601695dc9ea37206e9b7e977aebed. Reuse what fits rather than blindly reverting unrelated work.

Initialize the relevant span-name extractors, attributes extractors, operation-metrics factories, and dual-emission context customizers before configuration-dependent schema URL resolution and tracer/meter creation. Include components registered through instrumenter customizers. Keep the initialization hook visible where metrics factories or repository-owned decorators would otherwise hide it, including `OperationMetricsUtil` and Dubbo's wrapped span-name path. Keep any unavoidable wrapper-specific handling small rather than adding a general wrapper-discovery framework.

Remove the now-redundant explicit initialization and intermediate variables from gRPC and the other affected RPC construction sites, using the common instrumenter initialization path wherever it can own the lifecycle. Cover module-specific configurable helpers such as `GrpcAttributesExtractor` and the existing instance-owned AWS RPC extractors. Keep the existing public RPC factory signatures unchanged, use in-place initialization rather than configured copies, and do not introduce public `OpenTelemetry` factory parameters.

Preserve instance ownership, harmless repeated initialization with the same instance, and rejection of rebinding a helper to a different instance without corrupting an already-built instrumenter. Preserve standalone helpers' global/default-backed behavior without allowing that fallback to block their first explicit initialization. Keep the PR's instance-scoped RPC and service-peer selection, matching span names, attributes, metrics, units and schema URLs, and nested legacy child-metrics fix. Leave unrelated convention domains unchanged.

Adapt the focused tests, especially `RpcInstanceSemconvTest`, to prove that normal instrumenter construction configures helpers without caller-side initialization. Retain independent-instance legacy/preview/dual-emission coverage, same-instance reuse, cross-instance rejection, standalone behavior, customizer registrations, and the affected wrapped span-name path. Update the PR description only where it has become stale about initialization responsibilities. Work only on this PR's scope, preserve its current draft state, and commit and push to its existing head branch. Do not reply to real-user review comments or resolve review threads.

@copilot Reduce the diff in this existing PR without changing behavior, public APIs, instance ownership, or test coverage. Apply only the following three reductions, preserving all other existing and concurrently delivered changes.

1. In `instrumentation/aws-sdk/aws-sdk-1.11/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/awssdk/v1_11/internal/AwsSdkInstrumenterFactory.java`, keep `defaultAttributesExtractors` and `extendedAttributesExtractors` initialized at their field declarations in their original positions, changing those fields from `static final` to instance `final`. Remove the corresponding constructor assignments. `createAttributesExtractors(boolean)` does not depend on constructor state. The intended result is the same instance-owned lists with only the two `static` removals relative to the PR base, rather than moving initialization into the constructor. Preserve the already-reduced AWS SDK 2.2 factory diff.

2. Restore the original inline `GlobalOpenTelemetry.get()` calls and remove the introduced local variables and now-unused `OpenTelemetry` imports in these four files: `instrumentation/gwt-2.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/gwt/v2_0/GwtSingletons.java`; `instrumentation/rmi/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rmi/client/RmiClientSingletons.java`; `instrumentation/rmi/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rmi/server/RmiServerSingletons.java`; and `instrumentation/spring/spring-rmi-4.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spring/rmi/v4_0/SpringRmiSingletons.java`. These files currently only extract the global instance into locals. The builder still receives the same owning instance with the original inline calls. These four files should disappear from the PR diff.

3. In `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/`, restore the pre-PR Javadoc text for `RpcClientMetrics.get()`, `RpcServerMetrics.get()`, and `RpcMetricsContextCustomizers.dualEmitContextCustomizer()`. Their documentation rewrites are unrelated to instance scoping, and the original descriptions remain accurate. Restore the pre-PR parameter name and its use only in the `RpcSpanNameExtractor.create()` factory, rather than retaining the unrelated parameter rename. Keep the current span-name extractor Javadoc and all functional changes. Use the PR's merge base to identify original text, not the current tip of main.

Do not remove or redesign the common builder's initialization lifecycle, the internal initialization interface, configuration selection, metrics compatibility guards, test-import migrations, or focused instance-isolation and reuse tests. Preserve standalone global/default fallback, same-instance idempotence, cross-instance rebinding protection, service-peer selection, matching span/metric schema URLs, and the nested legacy child-metrics fix. Keep the explicit initialization before span-name customization in Dubbo and Thrift, including any explanatory comments added there. Do not change unrelated convention domains or add global-selection overloads to reduce test diffs.

Validate with the narrowest relevant existing formatting and test tasks. Review the final diff to confirm these are lossless reductions and that no tests or assertions were removed. Commit and push to this PR's existing head branch, preserve its current draft/ready state, and do not open a separate PR, reply to real-user review comments, or resolve review threads.

Not sure we should bother with synchronization and volatile here. We know that `initialize` is going to be called at most once before this component is actually used. If it gets called more than once it is a coding error.

@copilot Apply all of the following small, lossless diff reductions to this existing PR. Preserve behavior, public APIs, instance ownership, initialization timing, error handling, and test coverage. These are additional reductions after commit d782a01f5886dea15a90c8bef708b95ce10387ae; retain the earlier reductions and all other existing changes.

1. In `instrumentation-api/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/instrumenter/InstrumenterBuilder.java`, remove the newly introduced local variables in `addAttributesExtractor`, `addContextCustomizer`, and `addOperationMetrics`. Call `initializeOpenTelemetry` on each existing parameter, then retain that method's original collection-registration statement with its original `requireNonNull` call and message. The helper's `instanceof OpenTelemetryConfigurable` check is already a no-op for null, so the original null rejection remains intact and a failed initialization still cannot register the component. For example, `addOperationMetrics(OperationMetrics factory)` should call `initializeOpenTelemetry(factory);` followed by `operationMetrics.add(requireNonNull(factory, "operationMetrics"));`. Preserve every initialization hook, the helper itself, customizer handling, and the order of initialization before registration. The expected overall file diff is approximately +13/-0 rather than +21/-3.

2. In `conventions/src/main/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/StaticImportFormatter.kt`, use the existing `Rule.filePattern` mechanism to exclude exactly `SemconvRpcStabilityUtil.java` and `SemconvServiceStabilityUtil.java` from the `SemconvStability` rule. Use an anchored negative-lookahead filename regex with the same effective exclusions. Remove the new `excludedFiles` property, its two-file set, and its extra processing branch. Do not remove the exemptions or change any other formatter rule. This should reduce the file's PR diff from six added lines to approximately one.

3. In `instrumentation-api/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/internal/SemconvStability.java`, retain the identical two-line TODO about eventually replacing the `OpenTelemetry` parameter with `ConfigProvider` once for the related method group instead of repeating it on all five methods. Preserve its information and leave all methods and functional changes untouched. Do not remove the separate comments in other classes.

4. In `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/RpcSpanNameExtractor.java`, retain the original multi-line factory Javadoc wording, but remove the legacy-only span-name format so that it remains accurate for both old and preview naming. Use:

```java
/**
 * Returns a {@link SpanNameExtractor} that constructs the span name according to RPC semantic
 * conventions.
 */
```

This should change just the original format-description line rather than replace the entire Javadoc with `Creates the RPC span name extractor.` Keep the already-restored `attributesExtractor` factory parameter name and every functional change.

5. Remove only the unused `when(configProvider.getGeneralInstrumentationConfig()).thenReturn(general);` stub from each of these two new tests: `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/RpcInstanceSemconvTest.java` and `instrumentation/apache-dubbo-2.7/library-autoconfigure/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/apachedubbo/v2_7/DubboTelemetryBuilderTest.java`. General semconv configuration is read directly from `ExtendedOpenTelemetry`, which both tests already stub separately. The common builder uses `ConfigProvider` for the `"common"` configuration. Keep the provider mock, `getConfigProvider()` stub, provider's `"common"` stub, the direct `openTelemetry.getGeneralInstrumentationConfig()` stub, and all tests and assertions.

Limit changes to these six files and these specific reductions. Do not remove or redesign the builder lifecycle, internal initialization interface, configuration selection, metrics compatibility guards, test-import migrations, instance-isolation tests, or reuse/rebinding tests. Preserve global/default fallback for standalone components, same-owner idempotence, cross-owner rebinding protection, service-peer selection, span/metric schema URLs, the nested legacy child-metrics fix, the AWS factory reductions, and the explicit pre-wrapper initialization and explanatory comments in Dubbo and Thrift.

Run the narrowest relevant existing formatting and test tasks, applying formatting before behavioral validation. Check the final diff against this PR's merge base, not the current tip of main, to confirm that the reductions are lossless and no assertions were removed. Commit and push to this PR's existing head repository and branch, preserving any concurrent changes and its current ready-for-review state. Do not create another PR, post replies to real users, resolve threads, or request a review.

@copilot Move `RpcSemconvSelection` into the accessible internal package `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.api.incubator.semconv.rpc.internal` and reuse it from `instrumentation/grpc-1.6/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/grpc/v1_6/GrpcAttributesExtractor.java` instead of duplicating semantic-convention selection and initialization bookkeeping there.

Make only the helper types and methods needed across package/module boundaries accessible, and document the helper as internal and unsupported according to repository conventions. Update its existing RPC consumers to use the moved helper. Keep the separate gRPC extractor for gRPC-specific status codes and metadata; replace only its duplicated selection state and initialization/rebinding logic with delegation to the shared helper.

Preserve instance-scoped old/preview/dual-emission behavior, global/default fallback before explicit initialization, same-instance initialization idempotence, and rejection of rebinding to a different instance without corrupting the original selection. Preserve builder-managed initialization, public RPC factory signatures, emitted attributes, metadata filtering, and all unrelated behavior. Keep `DubboTelemetryBuilderTest.java` deleted as in commit `4a87657b2894eba4aefd7665ac2cdae54fd9cd57`.

Adapt relevant existing tests as needed and run the narrowest formatting and behavioral validation covering the moved helper and gRPC integration. Limit the change to this refactoring and its directly related consumers/tests. Commit and push to this existing PR's head branch, preserve its current ready-for-review state, and do not request a review, reply to real-user review comments, or resolve threads.

[Testing] This test checks metric names and schema URLs, but not the instance-specific method conversion. With an old-only global configuration, a dual-emitting instance whose context customizer still uses global selection would record `Service/Method` on the legacy histogram instead of `Method`, and these assertions would pass. The existing metrics tests use uninitialized factories and customizers, so they cover the global fallback rather than this path. Assert each histogram's attributes and unit here for both client and server.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly with two focused initialization changes. In `instrumentation-api/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/instrumenter/InstrumenterBuilder.java`, remove the redundant `initializeOpenTelemetry(spanNameExtractor)` call immediately after `applyCustomizers(this)` in the private `buildInstrumenter()` method. Keep initialization in the builder constructor and in the `setSpanNameExtractorCustomizer()` callback. The constructor initializes the original extractor before a customizer can wrap it and hide its internal initialization interface; the callback initializes replacements.

In `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/internal/RpcSemconvSelection.java`, retain the harmless same-OpenTelemetry-instance early return and add a short source comment explaining why it is intentional: a span-name customizer can return the original extractor, causing it to be initialized again, and components can be reused by instrumenters with the same owning instance. Keep the comment about the current lifecycle, not the history of this change.

Preserve different-instance rebinding rejection, the original component's configuration after rejection, standalone global/default fallback, and initialization before schema URL resolution and tracer/meter creation. Keep the existing pre-wrapper initialization in Dubbo and Thrift. Do not remove other initialization hooks, change synchronization or volatile behavior, redesign the lifecycle, or make unrelated changes. Retain focused coverage of same-instance reuse and customizer registration, and cover a customizer that returns the original extractor if the existing tests do not exercise it.

Commit and push to this PR's existing head branch, preserve its current draft/ready state, and do not create a follow-up PR. Do not reply to real-user review comments or resolve review threads.

@copilot Address the remaining synchronization concern in this existing PR. In `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/internal/RpcSemconvSelection.java`, remove `synchronized` from `initialize(OpenTelemetry)` and `volatile` from the `selection` field. This is a deliberate follow-up to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20474#discussion_r4317073496, whose instruction to leave those modifiers unchanged is superseded only for this focused change.

Document the initialization contract on `instrumentation-api/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/internal/OpenTelemetryConfigurable.java`: initialization happens during construction/configuration, before the component is used and before its owning instrumenter is safely published to other threads; callers must not initialize concurrently or race initialization with use. Explain concisely that visibility of initialized state relies on publication of the initialized instrumenter, not on a guarantee that initialization is called only once. Keep documentation about the current contract rather than the history of this change.

Keep same-instance initialization idempotent, including the existing source comment about customizers that return the original extractor and components reused with the same owner. Keep different-instance rebinding rejection without corrupting the original selection and preserve standalone global/default fallback. Retain builder constructor and customizer-callback initialization, the removal of the redundant build-time call, and the explicit pre-wrapper initialization in Dubbo and Thrift. Do not introduce replacement synchronization, concurrent reconfiguration support, a new lifecycle, public factory parameters, or unrelated changes.

Preserve the existing focused tests for independent instance-scoped semantic conventions, same-instance reuse, customizers returning the original extractor, and different-instance rejection. Validate the affected behavior using the repository's focused checks. Commit and push directly to this PR's existing head branch and preserve its current draft/ready state. Do not create a follow-up PR, reply to Laurit's or any other real user's review comments, or resolve review threads.

@copilot Address the coverage gap identified in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20474#discussion_r4316852405 directly in this existing PR. Extend `instancesEmitIndependentSemconv(boolean client)` in `instrumentation-api-incubator/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/rpc/RpcInstanceSemconvTest.java` to assert the exported duration histogram points' exact attributes and each histogram's unit. Keep the existing client/server parameterization and the legacy-only, preview-only, and dual-emitting instances, along with their existing span, metric-name, and schema-URL assertions.

For every emitted legacy `rpc.client.duration` or `rpc.server.duration` histogram, expect unit `ms` and exactly `rpc.system="test"`, `rpc.service="package.Service"`, and `rpc.method="Method"` on the recorded point. For every emitted preview `rpc.client.call.duration` or `rpc.server.call.duration` histogram, expect unit `s` and exactly `rpc.system.name="test"` and `rpc.method="Service/Method"` on the recorded point. Assert the recorded point count as well through the existing histogram assertion idioms. These are the attributes retained by `RpcMetricsAdvice` for this fixture; do not copy the additional span-only service-peer or error attributes into metric expectations.

The important regression is the dual-emitting instance when the global selection is old-only: the instance-configured context customizer must save the legacy method and the legacy histogram must replace `Service/Method` with `Method`. Metric names and schema URLs alone do not detect a customizer accidentally using global fallback. The standalone client/server metrics tests use uninitialized factories and customizers and therefore do not cover this instance-specific initialization path. Strengthen the existing test rather than adding another test class, configuration matrix, production abstraction, or production behavior change. Keep short expected values directly in assertions.

Limit the change to this test coverage and necessary imports. Preserve all existing production code, initialization/publication contracts, and unrelated tests. Run the focused `RpcInstanceSemconvTest` through the module's existing `test`, `testPreviewSemconv`, and `testBothSemconv` tasks, applying the repository's narrow formatting task first. Commit and push to this PR's existing head branch, preserve its current draft/ready state, and do not create a follow-up PR, post review replies, or resolve review threads.
